A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SysCaps research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including v3's added Appendix C.

before.justification: v2 reports original caption-quality, surrogate-accuracy and generalization experiments for building energy consumption and wind-farm generation in Sections 6.1–6.5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional ablation results and individual test predictions.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the caption-generation pipeline, text and sequence encoders, prediction architecture and squared-error objective. BERT fine-tuning was already specified in v2; the new frozen-BERT experiment is an ablation, not a revision of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same building-energy and wind-farm regression tasks using Buildings-900K/EnergyPlus and FLORIS data. Caption-length, synonym and design-space scenarios are retained. Appendix C adds examples within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Section 6.2 adds a frozen-BERT SysCaps-nl comparison, and Table 5 adds SysCaps-nl* without prompt augmentation. Existing LightGBM, one-hot and SysCaps comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v3 introduces ablation settings that disable BERT fine-tuning or wind-caption prompt augmentation. Existing dataset splits, NRMSE metrics and hyperparameter-search grids are retained.

E4.justification: New ablations examine the importance of text-encoder fine-tuning and the contribution of prompt augmentation. Appendix C adds building and wind-farm prediction case studies. Earlier caption-generalization, attribute-removal, design-space and caption-error analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both retain three-seed averages and the same uncertainty-reporting format in the main comparisons. The added Table 5 control follows that practice; no changed run count or new statistical estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds frozen-BERT stock-annual NRMSE of 0.356 and unaugmented wind SysCaps-nl* NRMSE of 0.038 ± 0.001. Table 5 revises augmented SysCaps-nl from 0.036 ± 0.001 to 0.035 ± 0.001. Tables 1–4 remain numerically unchanged, while Figures 12–13 add individual test predictions.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, model definitions and training objective in Sections 3 and 5, and the metric equations in Appendix A.1, are unchanged. Neither version presents theorem or proof contributions.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the main claims about language interfaces, surrogate accuracy, caption generalization and augmentation-based regularization. The introduction's reference to fine-tuned rather than pretrained embeddings clarifies an already-described procedure.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 newly interprets the frozen-BERT result as evidence that fine-tuning supports multimodal alignment. The conclusion explicitly acknowledges that no user studies were conducted and discusses simplifying technical descriptions and obtaining nonexpert feedback.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2.1 newly documents attribute-classifier heads, unfrozen encoder weights, AdamW learning rate 3e-4, batch size 128, maximum 100 epochs and stopping patience 5. The introduction replaces a future release promise with a stated code/data release and repository link.

R1.justification: The reference list contains the same works. Related-work wording changes preserve the positioning relative to LLM regression, multimodal timeseries models and knowledge-enhanced PDE surrogates.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify experiment organization and model comparisons. Author order and affiliations are updated, Appendix B is renamed, Appendix C is added, and the short broader-impacts paragraph is removed. The main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 12–13 and expands Table 5 with a control row and explanatory caption. Existing diagrams and plots are retained, with some appendix figures repositioned, table captions revised and local layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 claimed benefits from prompt augmentation without reporting a no-augmentation control; v3 supplies that comparison and adds evidence about fine-tuning. Classifier implementation details, release access information and explicit acknowledgment of absent user studies improve reproducibility and transparency. These targeted gains outweigh the small loss of the brief broader-impacts discussion.
